# Technical Description: Modular Bottle Trap Assembly

### 1. Main Body Architecture and Base Geometry
The bottle trap assembly is constructed around a main housing body designed for optimal fluid dynamics and spatial efficiency. The upper section of the body features an open end configured to attach directly to a vertical tailpiece pipe from a sink or basin. 

Opposite the open end, the main body transitions into a tapered, closed lower extremity terminating in an inclined face. Integrated directly into this inclined surface is at least one sealable drain orifice. This drain feature allows for convenient clean-out access, debris removal, and complete fluid evacuation without requiring the full disassembly of the trap housing.

### 2. Internal Trap Element Configuration
A specialized cylindrical trap element is mounted at the open upper end of the assembly. Extruding downwards along the longitudinal axis of the housing, this internal cylinder extends into at least half of the total overall length of the main body. This deep axial extension ensures the maintenance of a consistent, robust water barrier within the chamber, effectively preventing sewer gases from migrating back up through the plumbing system.

### 3. Discharge Port and Coupling Mechanisms
Fluid exits the assembly via an outlet orifice integrated into the side wall of the main body. Positioned strictly perpendicular to the vertical axis of the housing, this outlet connects to a standard horizontal drain pipe for discharge.

To optimize assembly, installation speed, and long-term reliability, the system incorporates thread-less couplings at both key interface points: the main body's open top end and the lateral outlet orifice. These thread-less joinery mechanisms form robust, leak-proof seals against the attached piping, mitigating common failure points associated with traditional threaded connections such as cross-threading or seal degradation.

---

### Summary of Key Features
* **Enhanced Maintenance:** Inclined, sealable drain port enables quick purging of sediment.
* **Effective Vapor Barrier:** Deep-reaching internal cylinder (≥50% body length) guarantees reliable hydraulic sealing.
* **Simplified Installation:** Thread-less couplings deliver secure, leak-free joints without complex threading.

# Technical Specification: Advanced High-Efficiency Bottle Trap Assembly

## 1. Executive Summary & System Background
Traditional plumbing trap designs—such as standard P-traps and conventional bottle traps—frequently suffer from installation inefficiencies, susceptibility to joint leaks, and cumbersome maintenance procedures. Standard threaded connections often cross-thread, overtighten, or degrade over time, leading to fluid seepage. Furthermore, clearing blockages typically requires the complete disassembly of the trap, risking structural wear and dynamic seal failure.

The advanced bottle trap assembly disclosed herein resolves these operational limitations. By incorporating a geometry optimized for fluid dynamics, a thread-less structural architecture, and an integrated maintenance port, this design delivers a high-reliability, leak-proof solution for residential, commercial, and industrial wastewater drainage systems.

---

## 2. Structural & Architectural Description

```
                 [ Sink Tailpiece ]
                        │
                        ▼
            ┌───────────────────────┐
            │   Thread-Less Inlet   │
            └───┐               ┌───┘
                │   Internal    │
                │  Cylindrical  │ ──► [ To Perpendicular
                │ Trap Element  │       Outlet Orifice ]
                │  (≥50% Depth) │
                │               │
  Main Body ──► │               │
                │               │
                └───────────────┘
                 \             /
                  \ Inclined  /
                   \ Closed  /
                    \  End  /
                     └──┬──┘
                        ▼
               [ Sealable Cleanout Orifice ]
```

### 2.1 Main Trap Body & Internal Architecture
The assembly comprises a rigid outer main body constructed from corrosion-resistant polymers or brass alloys. 

*   **Internal Cylindrical Trap Element:** Extending downward from the top inlet coupling, an internal cylinder projects vertically into the cavity of the main body. To ensure an effective hydraulic gas seal and prevent sewer gas backflow, this element extends **at least half (≥50%) of the total vertical length** of the main housing.
*   **Perpendicular Outlet Orifice:** Positioned on the lateral wall of the main body, a side discharge port extends horizontally (perpendicular to the vertical inlet axis) to channel wastewater directly into the wall-mounted drain line.

### 2.2 Tapered, Inclined Closed Base
Unlike standard flat-bottomed or spherical bottle traps, the lower boundary of the main body terminates in a **tapered, inclined closed end**. 

*   **Sediment Funneling:** The downward slope naturally directs heavier suspended solids, debris, and accidentally dropped items (such as jewelry) toward the lowest point of the incline.
*   **Flow Optimization:** The tapered walls reduce internal turbulence, allowing smooth fluid transition during high-volume discharge.

---

## 3. Key Innovations & Functional Performance

### 3.1 Thread-Less Coupling System
To eliminate the primary failure point of traditional plumbing—threaded compression nuts—the inlet and outlet ports utilize specialized **thread-less couplings**.

*   **Mechanism:** Connections are secured via push-fit, quick-connect, or snap-locking mechanisms paired with high-grade elastomeric O-rings (such as EPDM or silicone).
*   **Benefits:**
    *   **Speed:** Tool-free, rapid installation significantly reduces labor time.
    *   **Leak Prevention:** Uniform radial pressure ensures a permanent, vibration-resistant seal that will not back off under thermal expansion or structural movement.
    *   **Universal Compatibility:** Designed to interface seamlessly with standard smooth-walled tailpieces and horizontal waste pipes.

### 3.2 Integrated Drainage & Cleanout Orifice
Located directly at the lowest vertex of the inclined base is a dedicated **sealable maintenance orifice**.

*   **Seal Design:** Equipped with a removable, watertight cap (utilizing a quick-release bayonet or plug configuration with a dual-lip seal).
*   **Maintenance Efficiency:** For routine clearing of settled debris or liquid evacuation prior to servicing, technicians can unseal this bottom port directly into a collection vessel. This eliminates the need to disconnect the trap from the wall or sink tailpiece, preserving the integrity of the primary plumbing connections.

---

## 4. Method of Operation

1.  **Fluid Entry:** Wastewater enters vertically from the sink tailpiece through the top thread-less coupling into the internal cylindrical trap element.
2.  **Hydraulic Seal Formation:** Water exits the bottom of the internal cylinder near the lower half of the main body, filling the outer reservoir and forming a persistent water barrier against sewer gas infiltration.
3.  **Discharge:** Rising fluid flows upward through the annular space between the inner tube and outer body, exiting smoothly through the perpendicular lateral outlet.
4.  **Debris Collection & Maintenance:** Heavy particulates slide down the tapered, inclined base. During maintenance, opening the sealable bottom orifice instantly releases accumulated waste without disturbing the primary trap connections.

---

## 5. Conclusion
By uniting an inclined, self-funneling lower geometry, a extended internal trap seal, thread-less push-connect interfaces, and a dedicated bottom cleanout port, this bottle trap design offers superior structural integrity, zero-leak reliability, and unparalleled ease of installation and maintenance.

### INVENTION DISCLOSURE SUMMARY

**DOCKET NO.:** [Insert Firm/Internal Docket #]  
**DATE:** October 24, 2023  
**PREPARED BY:** [Attorney Name], Registered Patent Attorney  
**INVENTOR(S):** [Primary Inventor Name(s)]  

---

### I. TITLE OF THE INVENTION
**THREAD-LESS, QUICK-CONNECT BOTTLE TRAP ASSEMBLY WITH INTEGRATED MULTI-STAGE ELASTOMERIC SEALING AND MECHANICAL LOCKING RETENTION**

---

### II. TECHNICAL FIELD
This invention relates generally to plumbing fixtures and sanitary drainage systems, and more particularly to a thread-less, tool-free bottle trap assembly incorporating dynamic sealing structures and positive mechanical retention to prevent leakage and simplify installation in confined spaces.

---

### III. BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION & KNOWN PRIOR ART
Standard plumbing traps (e.g., P-traps and bottle traps) rely on threaded slip-joint connections secured by threaded nuts. These conventional designs suffer from several well-documented technical drawbacks:

1. **Cross-Threading & Alignment Errors:** In tight, under-sink spaces with limited visibility, installers frequently cross-thread plastic or metal nuts, damaging the threads and compromising structural integrity.
2. **Torque Inconsistency:** Under-tightening leads to immediate fluid leaks, while over-tightening frequently warps rubber washer gaskets or cracks the plastic housing, leading to catastrophic failure over time.
3. **Seal Degradation:** Traditional flat washers rely on axial compression. Thermal expansion, vibration, and pipe movement can cause these compressed washers to set, loosen, and leak.

There is an unmet operational need for a bottle trap system that completely eliminates threaded connections, provides tactile confirmation of a leak-proof seal, accommodates minor axial/angular misalignment, and allows for tool-free installation and maintenance clean-out.

---

### IV. SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION
The disclosed invention is an improved plumbing bottle trap featuring a completely **thread-less, push-to-connect interface** coupled with a **secondary twist-lock or snap-fit mechanical retention sleeve**. 

Instead of relying on rotational thread compression to form a seal, the invention utilizes a multi-stage radial sealing architecture combined with an internal/external locking mechanism. The assembly provides both **audible and tactile feedback** ("click-lock") to inform the installer that a fluid-tight seal and full mechanical engagement have been achieved without requiring any tools.

---

### V. DETAILED DESCRIPTION OF PREFERRED EMBODIMENTS

The bottle trap assembly comprises three main structural components: a **Trap Body (Sump Reservoir)**, an **Inlet Pipe Coupling**, and an **Outlet Pipe Coupling**. 

#### 1. Thread-Less Coupling Interface (Inlet & Outlet Ports)
* **Female Socket & Male Spigot Configuration:** Each connection port features a smooth bore female socket adapted to receive a smooth-walled male tailpiece or waste pipe.
* **Dual-Stage Radial Sealing System:** 
  * *Primary Seal:* An internal annular groove housing a high-durometer elastomeric Quad-Ring or O-ring designed to provide radial (rather than axial) sealing against the outer wall of the male pipe.
  * *Secondary Seal:* A downstream flexible elastomeric wiper lip seal designed to trap residual moisture, withstand backpressure, and prevent sewer gas egress even under micro-movements of the pipe.

#### 2. Positive Mechanical Retention Mechanism
To prevent accidental axial disengagement of pipes under hydraulic pressure or physical impact, the assembly incorporates a non-threaded locking system:
* **Option A (Push-Fit Collet with Release Ring):** An internal circumferential stainless-steel grab ring (collet) with angled teeth that allow forward insertion of the pipe but bite into the pipe wall upon reverse axial movement. A sliding release collar allows for intentional disassembly.
* **Option B (Cam-Latch / Bayonet Sleeve):** A external quarter-turn bayonet collar that slides over the joint, engaging outer detent pins on the trap body to lock the connection into a fixed axial channel with an integrated safety latch.

#### 3. Quick-Release Clean-Out Sump
* The bottom reservoir (the "bottle") attaches to the main upper housing via an **internal dual-O-ring bayonet lock** secured by a spring-loaded safety catch. This allows home occupants or plumbers to remove the trap bottom for cleaning without tools and without disturbing the inlet/outlet pipe connections attached to the wall or sink.

---

### VI. NOVEL AND PATENTABLE CLAIMS (KEY INNOVATIONS)

The core inventive concepts to be claimed in the forthcoming patent application include, but are not limited to:

1. **A thread-less plumbing trap assembly** comprising a housing defining a water seal chamber, at least one connection port including an internal radial seal, and a tool-free mechanical retaining structure configured to axially lock an inserted pipe.
2. **The multi-stage sealing architecture** incorporating both a primary radial compression seal and an auxiliary flexible lip seal arranged in series within a smooth-bore socket to accommodate axial expansion and angular deflection without loss of fluidic seal.
3. **The integrated clean-out reservoir connection** utilizing a quarter-turn bayonet mechanism featuring a tactile click-lock latch and dual radial seals to isolate wastewater without rotational thread stress.
4. **The visual/audible confirmation system** wherein the mechanical locking ring produces a distinct auditory sound and reveals a colored visual indicator band upon complete seating of the pipe.

---

### VII. COMMERCIAL & OPERATIONAL ADVANTAGES
* **Tool-Free Installation:** Reduces installation time by an estimated 60-70%. Ideal for DIY markets and professional plumbers working in restricted spaces.
* **Zero Risk of Thread Failure:** Completely eliminates cross-threading, stripped threads, and overtightening cracks.
* **Vibration and Thermal Resistance:** Radial dynamic seals absorb pipe thermal expansion/contraction and garbage disposal vibrations without loosening.
* **Streamlined Maintenance:** Quick-release bottom cap allows rapid retrieval of dropped items (e.g., jewelry) without disassembling the drainage network.

---

### VIII. PRIOR ART DISCLOSURE & NOVELTY CHECK
* *Has this invention been publicly disclosed, sold, or offered for sale?* [ ] YES  [ ] NO
* *Has any prototype been built and tested?* [ ] YES  [ ] NO
* *Are there known competing products using push-fit trap technology?* (Note: While push-to-connect pressure fittings exist for PEX/Copper supply lines, applying dual-stage radial sealing with bayonet retention specifically to DWV (Drain, Waste, Vent) bottle traps is believed to be novel).

---

### ATTORNEY ACTION ITEMS / NEXT STEPS
1. **Conduct a Formal Patentability Search (Prior Art Search)** targeting IPC/US Classes related to plumbing traps (E03C, F16L).
2. **Draft Utility Patent Application** emphasizing the structural interaction between the radial seals and the non-threaded retaining collar.
3. **Prepare High-Resolution Patent Drawings** illustrating cross-sectional views of the unseated vs. seated/locked positions.

---

# INVENTION DISCLOSURE STATEMENT (IDS)

**Date of Disclosure:** October 24, 2023  
**Title of Invention:** THREAD-LESS QUICK-RELEASE LEAK-RESISTANT BOTTLE TRAP ASSEMBLY  
**Primary Inventor(s):** [Inventor Name(s)]  
**Assignee/Company:** [Company Name / Individual Owner]  

---

## 1. FIELD OF THE INVENTION
This invention relates generally to plumbing fixtures and drainage systems, and more particularly to a bottle trap assembly incorporating a thread-less, tool-free mechanical coupling system that establishes a reliable, leak-proof seal without reliance on threaded fasteners or axial compression torque.

---

## 2. BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION & PRIOR ART

### Background
In plumbing systems, "bottle traps" (or waste traps) are installed beneath sinks and basins to retain a small volume of water, creating a fluid seal that prevents sewer gases from entering the living space. Standard bottle traps typically comprise an upper vertical inlet, a central bottle-shaped reservoir, an internal dip tube, an outlet pipe, and a removable lower cleanout cap.

### Problem Addressed
Conventional bottle traps rely on male-to-female threaded connections (often paired with flat rubber washers or tapered slip-joint washers) to secure the various housing components and cleanout caps. Threaded designs suffer from several major drawbacks:
1. **Cross-Threading:** Due to tight working spaces under sinks, users frequently cross-thread plastic or thin-walled metal components during installation, destroying the threads and causing permanent leaks.
2. **Inconsistent Gasket Compression:** Threaded joints rely on the installer’s physical torque. Overtightening can crush or tear rubber gaskets; undertightening leaves gaps, leading to slow micro-leaks.
3. **Debris Accumulation & Binding:** Mineral deposits, hair, and soap scum enter the thread grooves, causing the threads to bind, warp, or corrode, making periodic disassembly for cleaning extremely difficult.
4. **Shear Stress on Seals:** Rotating a threaded cap directly against a static rubber gasket introduces rotational friction (shear force), which can cause the gasket to bunch up or dislodge.

---

## 3. SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION

The present invention solves these problems by providing a **thread-less, quick-release bottle trap system** that decouples the *sealing function* from the *mechanical retention function*. 

Instead of helical threads, the trap utilizes a **push-and-twist bayonet or snap-fit latching mechanism** combined with **radial elastomeric O-ring seals**. Sealing is achieved entirely through radial compression within a smooth-bore receiving chamber, ensuring that the seal quality is predetermined by manufacturing tolerances rather than installation torque. 

The mechanical connection is locked via a spring-loaded sleeve or detent latch that prevents accidental disconnection due to water pressure spikes or physical vibration.

---

## 4. DETAILED DESCRIPTION OF PREFERRED EMBODIMENTS

### Components of the System
Referring to the conceptual architecture, the assembly comprises:
1. **Inlet Tube Receiver (Upper Housing):** Connects to the sink tailpiece.
2. **Main Trap Body:** The central fluid-retaining chamber housing the inner dip tube.
3. **Removable Lower Reservoir / Cleanout Cap:** The bottom cup designed to collect heavy debris.
4. **Thread-less Coupling Joint (The Novelty):** The interface between the Main Trap Body and the Lower Cleanout Cap (or between the Inlet Tube and the Trap Body).

```
        [ Sink Tailpiece ]
                │
                ▼
     ┌──────────────────────┐
     │   Upper Inlet Tube   │
     └──────────┬───────────┘
                │  <-- [Thread-less Radial Quick-Coupling]
     ┌──────────┴───────────┐
     │    Main Trap Body    │
     │                      │
     │  ┌────────────────┐  │──────► [To Wall Drain Outlet]
     │  │ Inner Dip Tube │  │
     └──┴───────┬────────┴──┘
                │  <-- [Thread-less Bayonet Locking Interface]
     ┌──────────┴───────────┐  <-- [Dual Radial O-Ring Seals]
     │ Removable Cleanout   │
     │     Bottom Cap       │
     └──────────────────────┘
```

### Mechanism of Operation

#### A. Dual-Stage Radial Sealing Interface
* The lower portion of the Main Trap Body terminates in a smooth, unthreaded male spigot possessing two circumferential channels holding a pair of elastomeric O-rings (e.g., EPDM or Silicone).
* The Lower Cleanout Cap comprises a corresponding smooth-bore female socket.
* Upon insertion, the O-rings are radially compressed against the inner wall of the female socket. Because engagement is strictly axial, no shear or twisting force is applied to the O-rings during installation.

#### B. Thread-Less Mechanical Retention (Bayonet / Latch System)
* **Lug-and-Track System:** The exterior of the male spigot includes diametrically opposed locking pins (lugs). The female socket includes corresponding "J-shaped" or "L-shaped" guide channels.
* **Push-Twist-Lock Action:** To assemble, the user aligns the lugs with the channels, pushes the cap upward vertically (compressing a internal wave spring or elastomeric dampener), twists 45 degrees, and releases. The spring pressure forces the lug into a locking notch at the end of the channel.

#### C. Secondary Anti-Rotation Safety Lock
* To prevent accidental opening (e.g., from children or impact), a sliding collar or snap-fit safety latch is integrated on the exterior rim. The latch automatically drops into engagement when the bayonet pin hits its locked position.
* Disassembly requires depressing the release tab and twisting in the reverse direction—requiring no wrenches or tools.

---

## 5. KEY NOVEL FEATURES & ADVANTAGES

* **Zero Risk of Cross-Threading:** Complete removal of helical screw threads eliminates thread stripping and misalignment during installation.
* **Pre-Calibrated Sealing (Leak Prevention):** Water tightness depends solely on the interference fit of the radial O-rings inside the smooth chamber. Seal compression is 100% controlled by factory dimensions, eliminating human error (over/under-tightening).
* **Tool-Free, Maintenance-Friendly Disassembly:** Allows non-professionals to remove the trap reservoir in seconds to clear clogs or clean out lost jewelry without damaging the plumbing.
* **Rotational Shear Elimination:** Seals slide axially into position, preventing gasket twisting, bunching, or premature tearing.
* **Vibration Resistance:** The detent locking pin/spring mechanism prevents the coupling from vibrating loose due to disposal units or water hammer effects.

---

## 6. PROPOSED CLAIMS FOR PATENT PROTECTION

1. **A plumbing bottle trap assembly, comprising:**
   * A trap body defining an internal fluid reservoir and an outlet port;
   * A removable lower cleanout cap;
   * A thread-less coupling mechanism securing the lower cleanout cap to the trap body, comprising at least one locking lug on an exterior surface and a corresponding track on an mating surface configured to receive the lug; and
   * At least one radial seal positioned between an outer wall of the trap body and an inner wall of the cleanout cap, wherein fluid sealing is independent of rotational tightening force.

2. **The bottle trap of claim 1,** wherein the track is a J-shaped locking channel providing a push-and-twist bayonet connection.

3. **The bottle trap of claim 1,** further comprising a biasing spring configured to apply axial force against the cleanout cap to hold the locking lug in a locked detent position within the track.

4. **The bottle trap of claim 1,** further comprising a spring-loaded safety latch slidably mounted to the exterior of the assembly to prevent counter-rotation of the cleanout cap when locked.

---

## 7. SUGGESTED DRAWINGS TO INCLUDE IN PATENT APPLICATION

* **FIG. 1:** Perspective view of the assembled thread-less bottle trap under a sink basin.
* **FIG. 2:** Exploded cross-sectional view showing the male spigot, dual O-ring grooves, female socket, and internal dip tube.
* **FIG. 3:** Detailed view of the J-track bayonet locking slot and locking lug engagement.
* **FIG. 4:** Close-up cross-section of the radial O-ring interface showing seal compression in the smooth bore chamber.

**ABSTRACT**

A drain connector assembly for joining a vertical tailpiece pipe to a horizontal drain pipe includes an adjustable housing having a vertical inlet port, a horizontal outlet port, and an articulating intermediate section defining a continuous fluid pathway. The vertical inlet port includes a quick-release compression collar configured to sealingly receive the tailpiece pipe. The horizontal outlet port includes a telescoping sleeve slidable to accommodate variable horizontal distances to the drain pipe. The articulating intermediate section comprises a sealed ball-and-socket joint that permits multi-axial angular alignment between the inlet and outlet ports while maintaining a constant cross-sectional flow area. An integrated elastomeric dynamic seal is disposed within the intermediate section to prevent leakage during adjustment. The assembly enables tool-free, leak-proof connection between misaligned vertical and horizontal drain components without requiring rigid pipe cutting or solvent welding.
